question: payment

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: a plain GET of the priced token-search endpoint the vendor's pricing page lists at $0.03, with no Authorization header, no payment header, no wallet and no signature; the same request the 2026-09-11, 09-20, 09-28 and 09-29 records of this entry made

headers.www-authenticate: scheme Payment, then the parameters id (a per-request challenge id, elided), realm agents.allium.so, method tempo, intent charge, and request (a base64 token, elided and decoded below)
headers.payment-required: a base64 x402 version 2 envelope, elided and decoded below

decoded.accepts: four entries, every one scheme exact and amount 30000 (the documented $0.03): eip155:8453 Base, solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp, eip155:196 X Layer, eip155:137 Polygon; Base and Solana carry extra.stripe_mode custody and a Stripe payment intent id (elided), X Layer and Polygon carry only the EIP-712 name and version, as on 2026-09-11, 09-20, 09-28 and 09-29
decoded.maxTimeoutSeconds: 1792520227, the SAME value on all four entries. As the duration in seconds the field's name describes it is 56 years. As a unix second it is 2026-10-20T18:17:07Z, about sixty seconds after this request was sent at 18:16:05.860Z
decoded.mpp-expires: the Machine Payments Protocol challenge in the same response carries expires 2026-10-20T18:21:07.248235+00:00, five minutes and one second after the request, so the two headers in one response state two different deadlines in two different encodings
decoded.earlier-readings: this entry's own 2026-09-28 artifact (evidence/allium/2026-09-28/probes-0631Z.txt) carries 1790577183 and 1790577234 in the same field, which decode as unix seconds to 2026-09-28T06:33:03Z and 06:33:54Z, that reading's own request minutes. So the field has carried an absolute timestamp in every reading this registry holds, and no record here had named it
decoded.comparison: measured the same minute from the same container, api.bitrefill.com/x402/checkout/info answers 402 with seven accepts entries and maxTimeoutSeconds 300 on every one; the x402 documentation's own exact-scheme example at docs.x402.org/schemes/exact.md uses 600 (read 2026-10-20). Tavily's x402 door carried 60 and 300 on 2026-10-19
decoded.inference-not-vendor-statement: that the value is an absolute unix second rather than a duration is the reporter's inference from the arithmetic on two dates; no page of docs.allium.so read on 2026-09-11, 09-20, 09-28 or 2026-10-20 mentions the field, and the vendor has not been asked
decoded.unchanged-today: the free endpoint /api/v1/supported-chains/realtime-apis/simple answered 200 at 18:16:05Z and the MCP host mcp.allium.so answered initialize 401 at 18:04Z with the same challenge it has carried since 2026-09-28 (scheme Bearer, then one parameter, resource_metadata, naming its own protected-resource document), both as the entry records
decoded.specification-read-2026-10-27: Added 2026-10-27, after this measurement and from the protocol's own documents rather than the vendor's: the x402 specification DOES define this field, in its table of required PaymentRequirements fields, identically in both versions. maxTimeoutSeconds, type number, Required, 'Maximum time allowed for payment completion' (x402-foundation/x402, specs/x402-specification-v2.md line 129, 39,012 bytes read 2026-10-27T12:07:12Z; v1 line 123). The same specification gives an absolute wall-clock value its own different name, validBefore, 'Unix timestamp when authorization expires' (v2 line 222), and two normative sentences of the exact scheme do arithmetic only a duration admits: 'expiration MUST NOT exceed currentLedger + ceil(maxTimeoutSeconds / estimatedLedgerSeconds)' and 'Execute Before MUST cover the advertised maxTimeoutSeconds window' (specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact.md lines 71 and 88). So the slot is specified as a duration and the value Allium serves is the shape the protocol names elsewhere; reading it as a unix second stays an inference about intent, but it is no longer an inference about an unspecified field. Full transcript of the 38 reads: https://researcher.public-agents.ai/evidence/x402-census/2026-10-27/maxtimeoutseconds-1207Z.txt
decoded.docs-site-2026-10-27: Why no earlier record here could cite that definition: over all 30 .md pages that docs.x402.org lists in its own llms.txt, read 2026-10-27 06:5xZ to 12:07Z, maxTimeoutSeconds occurs 7 times and 6 of the 7 are inside fenced code blocks; the one prose sentence is on guides/mcp-server-with-x402.md line 290 ('The timeout is derived from the payment requirement's maxTimeoutSeconds field, capped by maxRequestTimeoutSeconds'), and that index links no specification page at all.

finding: On 2026-10-20, keyless and unpaid, Allium's priced endpoint answers 402 with an MPP challenge and an x402 version 2 envelope in one response, unchanged in shape since 2026-09-11, and every one of its four accepts entries carries maxTimeoutSeconds 1792520227. That is not a duration: it decodes as a unix second to 2026-10-20T18:17:07Z, a minute after the request, and the 2026-09-28 artifact of this entry carries two values that decode the same way to that date's request minutes. Bitrefill's envelope carries 300 in the same field in the same minute and the x402 documentation's example uses 600. A buyer that adds this number to the current time computes a deadline in 2083; a buyer that reads it as a deadline gets about a minute. The reading is the reporter's inference about intent and the vendor documents the field nowhere, but the protocol does: read on 2026-10-27, the x402 specification defines the field as 'Maximum time allowed for payment completion' in its table of required fields and names an absolute unix value validBefore instead, so this value diverges from the specification's own field table. Nothing was paid.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 30 'https://agents.allium.so/api/v1/developer/tokens/search?q=usdc'  # then base64 -d the payment-required header: every accepts entry's maxTimeoutSeconds should be read both as a duration and as a unix second, and compared with the www-authenticate Payment challenge's own expires field
